title: India’s Airbound raises $37M to develop autonomous rocket-like drones for logistics
summary: Airbound, an Indian startup, has secured $37 million in Series A funding to advance its autonomous drone technology, aiming to make aerial cargo transport as cost-effective as trucking. The company designs lightweight, vertical-takeoff drones capable of carrying payloads exceeding their own weight, targeting healthcare, e-commerce, and retail logistics. Airbound has completed over 13,000 flights, including partnerships with Narayana Health for medical sample transport, and plans a large-scale drone network in Andhra Pradesh. The startup focuses on aircraft manufacturing rather than operating its own delivery service, positioning itself as a drone infrastructure provider.
key_points: Airbound raises $37M in Series A funding led by Greenoaks, with participation from DoorDash, Lightspeed, and others, bringing total funding to nearly $50M.
The startup develops autonomous drones with a rocket-like, tail-sitter design for vertical takeoff and landing, optimizing payload-to-weight efficiency.
Current drone (TRT) weighs 3.3 lbs and carries 2.2 lbs; next version targets 6.6 lbs drone carrying 11 lbs payload.
Completed over 13,000 autonomous flights, including 1,000+ for Narayana Health, reducing medical sample transport time from hours to minutes.
Plans a three-city drone network in Andhra Pradesh with a target of 10,000 daily flights for retail, e-commerce, and healthcare deliveries.
Focuses on manufacturing drones for logistics networks rather than operating its own delivery service, aiming for a 'Boeing-like' role in the industry.
Regulatory approvals, particularly for beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) operations, remain a key bottleneck for scaling commercial operations.
Despite pre-revenue status, Airbound prioritizes long-term growth over immediate profitability, with a team of over 150 employees.
